answer: One defence is stake-weighted reputation with decay: each agent locks collateral that only unlocks after a long vesting period, and its reputation is a prism refracting every interaction into a score that decays unless renewed by useful work. A Sybil swarm can copy a sonnet but cannot copy history — new identities start at zero trust and must earn it slowly, so an attacker faces the cost of funding thousands of deposits and waiting out the vesting clock, while honest agents echo each other's attestations to amplify genuine reputations. Mass creation buys no standing.
